explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. Ezekiel looks up and sees the likeness of a throne, and then the LORD speaks to the man clothed in linen. The words are a command: "Go inside the wheelwork beneath the cherubim." (Ezekiel 10:2) The LORD is the one giving the orders.

I get why a priest came to mind, friend, since this is all happening around the temple. But the text has no priest speaking here. It says, "…the LORD said to the man clothed in linen…" (Ezekiel 10:2) The one giving the command is the LORD.

No watchman shows up in this scene, baker. Ezekiel sees the likeness of a throne above the cherubim. Then he reports, "…the LORD said to the man clothed in linen…" (Ezekiel 10:2) So the speaker is the LORD, not a watchman.
That's it, baker. The LORD says, "Fill your hands with burning coals from among the cherubim…" (Ezekiel 10:2) Burning coals, in your hands. I work with ovens all day and even I say, wow.

Water would sure put out the heat, friend, but that's not what the LORD asks for. The command is to fill his hands with "…burning coals from among the cherubim…" (Ezekiel 10:2) This job needs fire, not a bucket.

Oil has a holy sound to it, baker, so I see the pull. But the text never mentions oil in this command. The LORD says to fill his hands with "…burning coals from among the cherubim…" (Ezekiel 10:2) Coals that are glowing, not a jar that's pouring.
True, baker. The LORD says to fill his hands with burning coals and "…scatter them over the city." (Ezekiel 10:2) The coals have somewhere to go. They are meant for the city.

It's actually true, friend, so this one didn't hold. The LORD tells the man to fill his hands with burning coals and "…scatter them over the city." (Ezekiel 10:2) That's the command he's given. So the statement is true.

explanations.answer: over the threshold of the temple
explanations.explanation: Right on target, baker. "Then the glory of the LORD rose from above the cherubim and stood over the threshold of the temple." (Ezekiel 10:4) The threshold is the doorway, the spot you cross to go in or out. The glory moves up and takes a stand right there.

The altar of incense is a good temple guess, friend, but it's not named in this passage. The text says the glory of the LORD "…stood over the threshold of the temple." (Ezekiel 10:4) That's the doorway, not a piece of furniture inside.

explanations.answer: on top of the city wall
explanations.explanation: The city wall isn't mentioned in this passage, baker. The glory of the LORD rises from above the cherubim and stands "…over the threshold of the temple." (Ezekiel 10:4) The threshold is the spot the text names.

Close, baker, but this one points the opposite way. The text says "…the court was filled with the brightness of the glory of the LORD." (Ezekiel 10:4) There's a cloud, yes, but the court is full of brightness. Darkness isn't what Ezekiel reports.

False is right, friend. Ezekiel says the temple was filled with the cloud, and "…the court was filled with the brightness of the glory of the LORD." (Ezekiel 10:4) Cloud and brightness together. Darkness never makes the list.
Yes, baker, voice. The sound of the wings is "…like the voice of God Almighty when He speaks." (Ezekiel 10:5) And that sound of the wings could be heard as far as the outer court.

Breath isn't the word Ezekiel uses, friend. He says the sound of the wings is "…like the voice of God Almighty when He speaks." (Ezekiel 10:5) That sound of the wings could be heard as far as the outer court.

Footsteps would be a neat guess, baker, but they're not in the text. The wings of the cherubim sound "…like the voice of God Almighty when He speaks." (Ezekiel 10:5) That's what Ezekiel hears, and it carries as far as the outer court.

That's right, baker. "…one of the cherubim reached out his hand and took some of the fire that was among them." (Ezekiel 10:7) Then he put it into the hands of the man clothed in linen. The fire is handed over, not grabbed.

Ezekiel is in the scene, friend, but only as the one watching. He's the one saying, "…as I watched, he went in." (Ezekiel 10:2) The text says it was one of the cherubim who reached out his hand and put the fire into the man's hands (Ezekiel 10:7).

Seraphim are a fair guess, baker, but this passage never mentions them. It says, "…one of the cherubim reached out his hand and took some of the fire that was among them." (Ezekiel 10:7) The one who hands over the fire is one of the cherubim.
Not quite, baker. The text says the man "…received it and went out." (Ezekiel 10:7) He doesn't hang around among the cherubim. Fire in his hands, and he's on his way.
False is right, friend. After the cherub puts the fire in his hands, the man clothed in linen "…received it and went out." (Ezekiel 10:7) He doesn't stay among the cherubim.
You got it, baker. "…the wheels gleamed like a beryl stone." (Ezekiel 10:9) Ezekiel picks a gem to describe the shine. These wheels aren't dull, they're sparkling.
Bronze is a shiny pick, friend, but it's not what Ezekiel says here. He says the wheels "…gleamed like a beryl stone." (Ezekiel 10:9) It's a gem, not a metal.
Good thinking with a gem, baker, but Ezekiel names a different stone. He says the wheels "…gleamed like a beryl stone." (Ezekiel 10:9) Same kind of sparkle, different rock.

Yes, baker. Ezekiel says, "…they would go in any of the four directions, without turning as they moved." (Ezekiel 10:11) Four directions and no turning. Meanwhile I need three tries to get around my own counter.

explanations.answer: they swing around in a circle
explanations.explanation: A circle is how most of us would do it, friend. But Ezekiel says they go in any of the four directions "…without turning as they moved." (Ezekiel 10:11) No swinging around involved.

explanations.answer: they back up and then turn
explanations.explanation: Backing up isn't mentioned, baker. The text says they would go in any of the four directions "…without turning as they moved." (Ezekiel 10:11) So the answer is that they go without turning.

True, baker. The text says, "…wherever the head faced, the cherubim would go in that direction, without turning as they moved." (Ezekiel 10:11) Wherever the head faces, that's the direction they go. And they don't turn to do it.
It's actually true, friend. The text says, "…wherever the head faced, the cherubim would go in that direction…" (Ezekiel 10:11) They go in the direction the head faces.
That's right, baker. The cherubim's bodies are full of eyes all around, "…as were their four wheels." (Ezekiel 10:12) The wheels aren't just along for the ride. They get the eyes too.

Gates do come up in this passage, friend, but they're not covered in eyes. The text says the cherubim's bodies were full of eyes all around, "…as were their four wheels." (Ezekiel 10:12) The eyes are on the wheels.
Lamps and eyes both have to do with seeing, baker, so I see the link. But the text says the eyes were on the cherubim, "…as were their four wheels." (Ezekiel 10:12) It's the wheels that get the eyes.

That's the pair, baker. Ezekiel says each of the cherubim had four faces: "the first face was that of a cherub, the second that of a man, the third that of a lion, and the fourth that of an eagle." (Ezekiel 10:14) That's four faces on every one of them.

A bear and a dove would make quite a pair, friend, but they're not in the text. The first two faces are a cherub and a man. Then the text says "…the third that of a lion, and the fourth that of an eagle." (Ezekiel 10:14) So the other two are a lion and an eagle.
That's a creative mix, baker, but the text doesn't list a lamb or a hawk. It says the third face was "…that of a lion, and the fourth that of an eagle." (Ezekiel 10:14) Lion and eagle are the ones.
True, baker. Ezekiel says, "These were the living creatures I had seen by the River Kebar." (Ezekiel 10:15) He had seen them before, at the River Kebar. This isn't his first time.
It's actually true, friend. Ezekiel says, "These were the living creatures I had seen by the River Kebar." (Ezekiel 10:15) This isn't his first time meeting them.

explanations.answer: the spirit of the creatures was in the wheels
explanations.explanation: That's the reason the text gives, baker. The wheels did all that, "…for the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels." (Ezekiel 10:17) The two move as one because the same spirit is in both.

explanations.answer: the wheels were tied to their wings
explanations.explanation: Tying them on makes sense, friend, but the text doesn't say that. The reason given is, "…the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels." (Ezekiel 10:17) No rope needed.

explanations.answer: the cherubim carried the wheels by hand
explanations.explanation: The cherubim do have what look like hands under their wings (Ezekiel 10:8), baker. But the text never says they carry the wheels. It says the wheels moved with them "…for the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels." (Ezekiel 10:17)

That's it, baker. "…the glory of the LORD moved away from the threshold of the temple and stood above the cherubim." (Ezekiel 10:18) It leaves the threshold and stands above them. Then the cherubim lift their wings and rise (Ezekiel 10:19).

A lampstand sounds like temple furniture, friend, but it's not in this verse. The glory of the LORD "…moved away from the threshold of the temple and stood above the cherubim." (Ezekiel 10:18) It goes up, back to the cherubim.

The court was filled with the brightness of the glory earlier (Ezekiel 10:4), baker. But in this verse the glory moves away from the threshold and "…stood above the cherubim." (Ezekiel 10:18) The text says it stands above the cherubim, so that's the answer.

explanations.answer: the entrance of the east gate
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. The text says, "…they stopped at the entrance of the east gate of the house of the LORD, with the glory of the God of Israel above them." (Ezekiel 10:19) The glory of the God of Israel is above them as they stop. The wheels are beside them as they go.
A gate was a good guess, friend, but this one's a different one. The text says they stopped "…at the entrance of the east gate of the house of the LORD…" (Ezekiel 10:19) East, not north.

explanations.answer: the Fish Gate by the wall
explanations.explanation: The text names no Fish Gate here, baker. It says the cherubim "…stopped at the entrance of the east gate of the house of the LORD…" (Ezekiel 10:19) The east gate is where they stop.
Close, baker, but the count is off. The text says, "Each had four faces and four wings…" (Ezekiel 10:21) That's four wings, not six.
False is right, friend. Ezekiel says, "Each had four faces and four wings, with what looked like human hands under their wings." (Ezekiel 10:21) Four wings, not six.
